mission.title: Install and Configure Linode Kubernetes Engine (LKE)
mission.description: Linode Kubernetes Engine (LKE) is a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies the deployment and management of Kubernetes clusters on Linode's infrastructure. It is ideal for users looking for a hassle-free Kubernetes experience with built-in integrations for Linode services. Key trade-offs include limited customization compared to self-managed solutions and potential costs associated with cloud resources.

steps.title: Install the Linode CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the Linode CLI, which is necessary for managing your Linode resources from the command line.

```bash

curl -sL https://github.com/linode/linode-cli/releases/download/v2.0.0/linode-cli-2.0.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -C /usr/local/bin

chmod +x /usr/local/bin/linode-cli

```

> This command downloads and extracts the Linode CLI to your PATH.
> Make the CLI executable.

steps.title: Create a Kubernetes Cluster
steps.description:
This step creates a new Kubernetes cluster on Linode with the specified version and node count.

```bash

linode-cli lke cluster-create --label my-cluster --region us-east --k8s-version 1.30 --node-count 3

```

> Replace 'my-cluster' with your desired cluster name.

steps.title: Set Up Kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures your kubeconfig file to connect to your new Kubernetes cluster.

```bash

linode-cli lke kubeconfig-view my-cluster --format yaml > ~/.kube/config

```

> This command saves the kubeconfig to your local machine.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This step checks the status of the nodes in your Kubernetes cluster to ensure they are running.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> You should see your nodes listed with a 'Ready' status.

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
This step sets up additional features like autoscaling and monitoring for your cluster.

```bash

kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/linode/linode-cloud-controller-manager/v0.9.6/deploy/ccm-linode-template.yaml

```

> This command deploys the Linode Cloud Controller Manager.

uninstall.title: Delete the Kubernetes Cluster
uninstall.description:
This step removes the Kubernetes cluster and all associated resources. Be aware that this will result in data loss.

```bash

linode-cli lke cluster-delete my-cluster

```

> Replace 'my-cluster' with your cluster name.

uninstall.title: Remove Orphaned Resources
uninstall.description:
This step ensures that any orphaned resources such as load balancers and DNS records are cleaned up.

```bash

linode-cli nodebalancer delete --label my-nodebalancer

```

> Replace 'my-nodebalancer' with your NodeBalancer name.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the Kubernetes Cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up your data. This step upgrades your cluster to a newer version.

```bash

linode-cli lke cluster-update my-cluster --k8s-version 1.30

kubectl get nodes

```

> Replace 'my-cluster' with your cluster name.
> Verify that the nodes are updated and in 'Ready' status.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates an issue with the kubeconfig file or cluster certificate.

**Fix:**
Regenerate the kubeconfig using 'linode-cli lke kubeconfig-view my-cluster --format yaml > ~/.kube/config'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'No resources found in default namespace'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that no resources have been deployed in the default namespace.

**Fix:**
Deploy resources using 'kubectl apply -f <your-resource-file.yaml>'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to create service: Service 'my-service' is invalid'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates a misconfiguration in the service definition.

**Fix:**
Check the service definition for errors and correct them.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient CPU resources available'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the cluster does not have enough resources to schedule the pod.

**Fix:**
Increase the node count or resize existing nodes.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for new NodeBalancer features and improved integration with Linode's API.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: No specific migration steps required for this version.

resolution.summary: You should see the output of 'kubectl get nodes' showing all nodes in 'Ready' status.

prerequisites.description: Ensure you have the Linode CLI installed and configured with your API token.
